items.title: A trivial Kan fibration of simplicial sets is a homotopy equivalence
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-trivial-kan-homotopy at source lines 5858-5862: every trivial Kan fibration f : X to Y of simplicial sets is a homotopy equivalence. The proof at source lines 5864-5880 uses the lifting property of the previous lemma to choose a right inverse g : Y to X, builds the square whose top horizontal map is (id_X, g f) on the boundary of the 1-simplex times X and whose bottom map is the composite through f and the projection Delta[1] to Delta[0], observes that the square commutes because f g f = f, and fills the dotted arrow by the lifting property again, which is precisely the required homotopy from g f to the identity. It is short; the substance is the correct bookkeeping of the two boundary copies of X and the use of the lifting property twice.
